title: Determination of bisphenol a migration from food packaging by dispersive liquid-liquid microextraction
author: Mahdavianpour, Chamkouri, et al.

steps.title: Prepare BPA stock and working standards
steps.instruction: Dissolve 5 g bisphenol A (BPA) in 50 mL methanol to obtain a 100 mg mL⁻¹ stock solution; prepare six working standards (0.009, 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 mg mL⁻¹) by diluting the stock with methanol.

steps.title: Store and filter solutions
steps.instruction: Store the stock solution and all working standards at 4 °C; bring them to room temperature before use and filter all solvents, standards, and samples through a 0.22 µm nylon filter (Varian, USA).

steps.title: Collect and homogenize food samples
steps.instruction: Obtain 24 packaged food items (canned, paper‑boxed, glass‑jarred) from local supermarkets, keep them at room temperature (± 25 °C), open the packages, homogenize the entire contents, and retain aliquots for analysis.

steps.title: Prepare tomato and fruit extracts
steps.instruction: Weigh 5.0 g homogenized tomato or fruit into a screw‑capped glass vial, add 3 mL ultra‑pure water, vortex 4–5 min, centrifuge 4000 × g for 2 min; add 5 mL acetonitrile, 2.0 g anhydrous MgSO₄ and 0.5 g NaCl, shake 15 min, centrifuge again 4000 × g for 2 min, transfer the supernatant to a volumetric flask and bring to 50.0 mL with ultra‑pure water.

steps.title: Prepare canned fish extracts
steps.instruction: Place 0.1 g canned tuna in a screw‑capped glass vial with 5.0 mL acetonitrile, homogenize in an ultrasonic bath for 30 min, centrifuge 1500 × g for 15 min, mix the extracted phase with 15 mL n‑hexane, transfer to a volumetric flask and dilute to 50 mL with ultra‑pure water, then adjust pH to neutral with 1 M NaOH.

steps.title: Prepare powdered milk extracts
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 g powdered milk and 2.5 mL 50 % (w/v) ethanol to a screw‑capped glass vial, degas in an ultrasonic bath for 3 min, centrifuge 5000 × g for 35 min, filter the supernatant, transfer to a volumetric flask and bring to 50 mL with ultra‑pure water, finally adjust pH to 7.0 with NaOH.

steps.title: Prepare juice and milk extracts
steps.instruction: Pipette 10.0 mL homogenized juice or milk into a glass vial, adjust pH to 7.6 with phosphate buffer, homogenize in an ultrasonic bath for 3 min, then filter the sample.

steps.title: Perform DLLME extraction and HPLC injection
steps.instruction: To each prepared sample inject 35 µL 1‑undecanol (extracting solvent) and 1500 µL acetone (dispersive solvent), mix in an ultrasonic water bath for 5 min, centrifuge at 6000 rpm for 5.0 min, collect the settled phase and inject it into the HPLC‑DAD system; no salt is added.

steps.title: Record method validation parameters
steps.instruction: Document the following validation data: LOD = 0.01 ng g⁻¹, LOQ = 0.08 ng g⁻¹, linear range = 0.009–25 ng g⁻¹, correlation coefficient = 0.9981, repeatability RSD < 5.2 %, enrichment factor = 1980 at 2 ng g⁻¹.

description: The widespread use of chemicals in the food industry can be a health danger for humans and animals (especially pets) [1,2]. Bisphenol A (BPA) as a common monomer is used to produce epoxy resins and polycarbonates [1]. BPA migration from packaging materials was identified in many packaged foods such as vegetables, soft drinks [1,2]. Chemical compounds, such as Bisphenol A (BPA), can be carcinogenic and damage the liver, bones, nerves, and also endocrine system [2,3]. Important properties of BPA comprise moderate water solubility, low vapor pressure, low volatility, and its solid state at ambient temperature [4]. So, because of differences between food industries around the world, it is necessary to monitor the presence of BPA in different packaged foods and different food brands [1], [2], [3], [4]. Several pre-concentration methods, such as liquid–liquid extraction (LLE), solid-phase extraction (SPE), and dispersive liquid–liquid microextraction (DLLME), have been developed to determine BPA [4], [5], [6], [7], [8]. DLLME is similar to LLE with an extraction solvent in the microliter range [4], [5]. DLLME is a novel and powerful pre-concentration method with a small volume of the disperser solvent and the extraction solvent. In the DLLME method, an appropriate mixture solvent is rapidly injected into the sample, and then, the mixture is gently shaken, and a cloudy solution containing fine droplets is dispersed in the sample solution [4]. The advantages of the DLLME method are short extraction time, fast preparation, low cost, low sample cleanup, and high enrichment factor. The main purpose of this work was to develop a simple, accurate, and sensitive method to measure BPA in different food samples, using HPLC-DAD after pre-concentration by the DLLME procedure.
